summary: Redwood AE/SE ran a hosted API demo focused on embeddings + reranking for Oceanscape's search relevance use case. Customer currently uses Elastic + Pinecone for hybrid search. Main concerns: relevance quality vs latency, cost of serving, and data security (KMS and SOC2). Redwood proposed a hosted pilot with embeddings + rerank pipeline, described rerank endpoint (cross-encoder style) vs vector-only, and walked through Console metrics and Optimize suggestions. Agreed next steps: send pricing and security docs, schedule pilot benchmark and technical deep dive.
topics: Embeddings generation options and model choices
Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, data retention
transcript: [00:00] Maya: Hi everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45 minutes; I'll let Jordan and Anika do the walkthrough and leave time for Q&A.
[00:12] Liam: Yep works for us. Quick intro - I'm Liam, CTO at Oceanscape, Sara heads search, Devon is our eng lead. We're excited to see how Redwood can help with relevance.
[00:25] Jordan: Great - quick agenda: current infra and pain points, demo of hosted embeddings and rerank endpoints, Console + Optimize, then pilot proposal.

[00:40] Sara: Our main problem is search quality on article recommendations. We currently use Elastic for classic BM25 and Pinecone for vectors. We're seeing drift and some latency spikes during peak traffic.
[00:55] Devon: We want to keep average p95 under 120ms for user-facing requests; cost is a big factor - we have budget constraints for per-query cost.
[01:10] Jordan: Understood. Quick qualification: how big is your corpus? you said articles - how many?
[01:18] Priya: About 500k documents, each ~200-400 tokens on average, plus we keep historical versions. Typical query load ~200 req/s with spiky peaks to 800 for special events.
[01:35] Jordan: Thanks. So use-case looks like: retrieve with vector store for recall then rerank top-K for precision - classic hybrid. That's exactly what we'll demo.
[01:48] Maya: I'll jump in on the business side: we support hosted, dedicated, and private. Today we'll demo hosted API - fastest to get going, with pilot options for higher isolation if needed.
[02:05] Liam: One quick security Q - do you support customer-managed keys? we need KMS integration and SOC 2 evidence.
[02:13] Anika: Yes we integrate with KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated; hosted can support envelope encryption and we have SOC2 Type II. We'll share the security packet after the call.
[02:25] Sara: Good. Show us the rerank approach - we're evaluating cross-encoder reranking vs doing nearest-neighbor on embedding similarity.

[02:35] Jordan: Cool - I'll switch over to the demo. (screen share) So first: embeddings endpoint. You post your document text or batched docs and we return a 1536-d vector by default - model choices shown in the catalog. Note: model names sometimes show as open variants, we labeled them in the UI as 'rw-embed-1536' for clarity.

[03:05] Jordan: Here's a simple curl example: POST /v1/embeddings with payload docs array. We support batching and streaming for large ingestions. Batching reduces cost but increases latency for single-doc ingestion.
[03:22] Devon: For ingesting 500k docs, any throughput guidance?

[03:28] Jordan: For hosted, we recommend the ingestion job using our bulk upload job in Console - typical throughput for 1536-d vectors is about 10-20k docs / minute depending on network. For dedicated you can tune more aggressively.
[03:45] Priya: And dimensionality - can we pick 1024 or 2048?
[03:48] Jordan: Yes, we offer multiple embedding models with different dims. Our Optimize tool can recommend a profile; for your use case 1536 is a good tradeoff.

[04:05] Jordan: Next, the rerank endpoint. Conceptually, you send the top-N candidate ids from your vector store and the query, and we return a reranked list using a cross-encoder style model - higher compute but much better precision on ranking.

[04:25] Jordan: Example flow: retrieve top-100 by vector similarity, then call /v1/rerank with query + candidates, we score and return top-K. Latency depends on K and model; for top-100 with our default rerank model p95 is ~140-220ms on hosted.
[04:46] Sara: 140-220ms - that's within our p95 window if we budget for it, but it's for a single rerank call; how does that scale at 200 req/s?

[04:58] Jordan: Good question. We recommend two options: 1) tuned hybrid where you reduce candidate set to top-20 before rerank, or 2) use a lighter-weight rerank model for high QPS. Redwood Optimize can suggest the right K and model combination based on a small benchmark.
[05:16] Devon: So Optimize will run experiments and recommend configs?
[05:19] Anika: Exactly - it uses your sample query set + gold labels or human evals. It will recommend batch sizes, candidate K, model variants, and whether quantization is a net win.
[05:33] Liam: How do you measure quality? we care about NDCG/precision@10 and latency.

[05:39] Jordan: We surface those in Console per-route: token usage, latency histograms, and a quality dashboard where you can plug evaluation sets to get NDCG/precision curves. We also provide regression alerts if quality drops after a model change.
[05:54] Sara: Can you show the Console?

[05:56] Jordan: (screen shows Console) Here is a per-route dashboard. You can see embeddings ingestion jobs, vector store connectors (we have out-of-the-box connectors for Pinecone and weav..wea- 'Weaviate' - sometimes transcript shows wierd), and rerank route metrics. You can also preview sample rerank results inline.

[06:20] Jordan: Quick demo: I run a sample query, retrieve top-50 from Pinecone (we simulate), then call rerank. Here's before vs after: before - top-5 has repeated topic drift; after rerank top-5 focuses on user intent more accurately.
[06:40] Sara: That's promising. One nuance: we use user signals for personalization; can the rerank incorporate user context or session signals?

[06:49] Jordan: Yes, you pass additional context fields with the query and candidates; rerank models can condition on that metadata. For PII-sensitive context, you can choose to hash or keep metadata out of hosted requests; private deployment offers full on-prem control.
[07:05] Liam: Cost - can you ballpark per-query cost for retrieve+rerank?

[07:11] Maya: Ballpark depends on K and model. For retrieve + top20 rerank using our default hosted rerank model, customers see X - (note: exact numbers we will put in the pricing doc). As a reference, a typical pilot run we propose budgets ~$2k-4k for testing and benchmarking depending on traffic and model choices.
[07:30] Devon: We will need a clearer estimate. Please include cost for heavy peak scenarios.
[07:35] Maya: Yes will do - action item.

[07:40] Jordan: Back to tech - about cold start and caching: Redwood supports prefix caching and KV cache for autoregressive models, but for rerank we support response caching for repeated queries and a soft TTL. That helps reduce cost for high-repeat queries.
[07:58] Priya: What's the data retention policy for hosted? We can't keep user PII beyond X days.

[08:04] Anika: Hosted has configurable retention and data deletion on request; we also have an option for no-persist where embeddings and intermediate artifacts are not persisted beyond the request (subject to model-specific constraints). We'll provide the exact retention SLAs in the security packet.
[08:20] Liam: For compliance, we need SSO/SAML and RBAC for Console access.
[08:25] Maya: We support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and RBAC at route and project level. We'll include setup docs.
[08:33] Sara: Any gotchas with Pinecone integration? we've seen mismatched vector dims before.
[08:39] Jordan: We have connectors that handle dim checks and will flag mismatches. For migration we offer a small shim and a migration checklist.
[08:50] [09:00] (Jordan runs a live rerank on a sample set)
[09:12] Jordan: Note the transcripts sometimes read model names slightly off; in the API it's exact. Also our SDKs have helpers for batching and retry semantics.
[09:25] Devon: For pilot, what does success look like?
[09:29] Liam: We want a 10-15% uplift in NDCG@10 and maintain p95 latency under 200ms for user queries. Also cost per query should not exceed our threshold - I'll put the exact number in the doc.
[09:42] Jordan: Great - that's measurable. We'll run a 2-week A/B with sample queries and real traffic routing to compare current system vs Redwood hosted rerank + embeddings.
[09:55] Sara: How much engineering effort on our side?
[10:00] Maya: For hosted pilot minimal: provide dataset, a query sample, and we can handle most ingestion and run benchmarks. For dedicated/private there is more configuration and infra work.
[10:10] Devon: What's the SLA for hosted during a pilot?
[10:13] Maya: Hosted has basic uptime SLA; Dedicated offers stronger SLA. We'll share a clear matrix in the pricing packet.
[10:20] Priya: Do you support model version pinning? we need reproducible rerank results for experiments.
[10:26] Jordan: Yes pin by model id and config. Console records the model version used per-route and you can roll back or do canary deploys.
[10:36] Liam: Any customer references in our media vertical?
[10:40] Maya: We have a couple of publishing customers (we'll send names and case studies), one had similar scale and ran a dedicated pilot for a month.
[10:50] Sara: On evaluation, can Optimize suggest quantization settings? we've seen smaller models do well when quantized.
[10:59] Anika: Yup Optimize will profile your workload and recommend quantization if it helps latency/cost without hurting accuracy; it ties into the regression alerts.
[11:10] Devon: What about rate limiting and quotas?
[11:13] Jordan: We expose per-key quotas and rate limits. For high QPS you can request reserved capacity or dedicated pools to guarantee throughput.
[11:24] Liam: Ok let's talk rough timeline: we want pilot before Black Friday traffic in late Nov. Are you able to start in October?
[11:32] Maya: Yes - if we sign pilot agreement in early October we can schedule ingestion and benchmarking during mid-October, run 2-week A/B in November.
[11:42] Sara: Good. Any blockers from security?
[11:45] Anika: We'll need your security contact to sign off on SOC2 docs and KMS arrangements; the hosted no-persist mode can help with PII concerns.
[11:55] [Crosstalk] Devon: We'll loop in infra; Liam will share the dataset link.

[12:05] Jordan: Quick note on rerank compute: Cross-encoder style is more expensive than dot-product re-ranking; we often do approximate approach - use a lightweight cross-encoder only on top-20. That's what we recommend for cost/latency.
[12:25] Sara: For analytics, can we export per-query traces? we want to correlate user sessions.
[12:32] Jordan: Console exposes traces and you can export logs to your S3 or SIEM. We support structured traces and tags.
[12:42] Liam: For pilot data, is there an NDA?
[12:46] Maya: Standard mutual NDA is fine - we can attach it to the pilot agreement.
[12:52] Priya: Any recommended evaluation metrics beyond NDCG? maybe MRR and click-through predicted lift.
[12:58] Jordan: Absolutely - Optimize dashboard supports NDCG, MRR, precision@k, and you can upload click labels to compute CTR lift.
[13:10] Devon: For the ingestion job, will Redwood transform docs (e.g., canonicalization)?
[13:16] Jordan: We have optional pre-processors: HTML stripping, token limits, and custom tokenizer hooks. We can share the ingestion notebook.
[13:28] Sara: Show a sample rerank response payload?

[13:33] Jordan: Sure - (shows JSON) each candidate gets a score field and normalized rank; we also return a debug snippet with why top candidates were chosen - note debug info can be turned off for privacy.
[13:49] Liam: One more on costs: do you charge for embeddings storage separately?
[13:54] Maya: Hosted charges include embeddings storage and queries; we'll show line items. For dedicated, storage may be part of committed capacity.
[14:05] Priya: Can we run offline rerank experiments without hitting production?
[14:09] Jordan: Yes - we provide an offline rerank API and a local SDK for batch scoring so you can run experiments on samples without affecting live traffic.
[14:22] Devon: We're concerned about model drift as our content changes; how frequently should we retrain or refresh embeddings?
[14:28] Anika: It depends, but we often recommend periodic full-reindexes monthly and incremental updates daily. Optimize can surface drift signals from query logs.
[14:40] Sara: Any comments about regional data residency? we need EU copies for EU users.
[14:46] Maya: We offer region pinning for hosted and private deployments for strict residency - we'll note regions in the security packet.
[14:58] Liam: Ok let's recap and next steps.

[15:02] Maya: Recap: Redwood demoed embeddings + rerank hosted flow, Console/Optimize capabilities, proposed pilot (2-week A/B) targeting 10-15% NDCG uplift and p95 latency under 200ms. Action items: Maya send pricing + pilot terms, Jordan send benchmark checklist + demo notebook, Devon share dataset and query set.
[15:20] Liam: That matches our notes. We'll expect the packet and pricing by Monday. Thanks everyone.
[15:28] Sara: Thanks all - looking forward to the pilot.
[15:30] Maya: Thanks - we'll follow up and set the next call. Goodbye.
[15:33] (meeting ends)
[15:35] NOTE: Transcript contains occasional mis-heard product names and minor ASR artifacts (e.g., 'Weav..wea' in place of Weaviate)
[15:40] LINKS SHARED: https://redwood.ai/pilot-templates, https://redwood.ai/security/soc2, sample-benchmark-notebook (shared by Jordan)
